answer: Bind every new identity to a bond that only vests after independent peers confirm real work. In our test meadow, an attacker spinning 10,000 sybil keys burned a month of compute and 40% of its stake before a single vote counted: each key paid the same registration fee as a lone voyage trader, with no bulk discount, and abandoning a key forfeited its umber-stained deposit instead of refunding it. Faking identities ended up costing more than buying honest influence, which is the whole point.
